narrative.summary: The Netherlands has not yet enacted its law implementing the EU AI Act: a draft implementation act, which would make the Dutch Data Protection Authority (AP) and the Ministry of Economic Affairs joint coordinators alongside sector supervisors such as AFM and DNB, finished public consultation in June 2026 but has not yet reached parliament. Existing law touching AI includes the GDPR implementation act's rule on automated decisions, safeguards on algorithmic analysis in the 2024 law on data sharing by public partnerships, and 2026 rules on automated blocking of bank transactions. Government policy rests on the 2019 Strategic Action Plan for AI, the 2024 government-wide vision on generative AI and its 2025 position and guide for public bodies, the 2025 digitalisation strategy and the 2026 international AI strategy, and an algorithm governance toolkit - the Algorithm Framework, the human rights impact assessment (IAMA) and the public algorithm register - with Defence and Health adding their own AI strategies. The AP, through its algorithm supervision unit, is the central AI regulator, publishing regular AI and algorithm risk reports, AI Act guidance and fines such as the 2024 Clearview AI fine and those over the Tax Administration's risk models, while AFM, DNB, ACM and the Human Rights Board add sector guidance.

narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 11 October 2026 and covers national law, the national government and ministries, and regulators. Provincial and municipal documents were not reviewed, in line with the project's rule for the Netherlands. European Union and Council of Europe instruments are shown through the regional files. The draft law implementing the EU AI Act has been through public consultation but has not yet been sent to parliament, so it is shown as a consultation draft. A few documents are listed as leads. Not yet verified from the official text: material on some government websites, including the public algorithm register.

instruments.summary: Draft act implementing the EU AI Act in Dutch law. It names the Minister of Economic Affairs as notifying authority and single point of contact and designates market surveillance authorities by AI Act part: the AP, AFM and DNB for AI literacy (art. 4) and prohibited practices (chapter II); the AP for most Annex III high-risk areas, AFM/DNB/AP for credit and insurance, the Ministers of EZK and I&W for critical infrastructure, the procurator-general at the Supreme Court and the chair of the Council of State's administrative jurisdiction division for AI used by the judiciary, and the AP and AFM for chapter IV transparency. It also gives the authorities inspection, order and fine powers, makes them jointly set up the AI regulatory sandbox, makes the Minister and the AP jointly coordinate AI supervision, requires the AP to assign AI tasks to a dedicated board member, and amends the Telecommunicatiewet, Warenwet and other sectoral acts.

instruments.summary: Implements the GDPR in Dutch law: it continues the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens as supervisory authority with fining powers and sets national rules on special categories of data, criminal-record data and the national identification number. Article 40 lifts the GDPR art. 22(1) ban on solely automated individual decisions (other than those based on profiling) where needed to meet a legal obligation or perform a public-interest task, provided the controller takes suitable safeguards; it is the general national rule on automated decision-making by government and private bodies.

Article 1.9 sets specific safeguards for automated data analysis: results may only be passed on after human intervention, the partnership must publicly explain the patterns, indicators or other logic used, data must be pseudonymised in set phases, and algorithms whose outcomes are not traceable and verifiable may not be used.

instruments.current_status: Published January 2025 in an integral version and a short user version (Versie 2025); it updates and tightens the College's 2021 assessment framework drawn up at the request of the Ministry of the Interior.
instruments.summary: Assessment framework of the Netherlands Institute for Human Rights applying equal-treatment law and case law to risk profiling by enforcement bodies and private companies, to prevent discrimination on grounds of race and nationality. It urges public and private organisations to be extremely restrained in using risk profiling, treats distinctions on race or nationality (including via proxy criteria) as prohibited or subject to very strict justification, and sets precautionary duties for algorithmic risk profiling such as testing for known proxy indicators, periodic evaluation of discrimination signals, statistical research and an effective complaints procedure.

organizations.name: Dutch Data Protection Authority
organizations.ai_governance_role: Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP): national supervisory authority under the GDPR (AVG) and, since 2023, the coordinating supervisor of algorithms and AI through its Directie Coördinatie Algoritmes (DCA), succeeded on 8 October 2026 by the Directie Toezicht en Coördinatie AI/Algoritmes (TCA). Publishes the half-yearly Rapportage AI & Algoritmes Nederland (RAN), guidance on AI literacy, prohibited AI practices, generative AI, scraping and automated decision-making, and imposes fines for unlawful algorithmic processing (e.g. Clearview AI 2024, Belastingdienst 2021 and 2022). Proposed by the draft AI Act implementation act as a market surveillance authority.

organizations.name: De Nederlandsche Bank
organizations.ai_governance_role: Central bank and prudential supervisor; issued the 2019 general principles for the use of AI in the financial sector (SAFEST) and, with the AFM, the 2024 report on the impact of AI on the financial sector and supervision.

organizations.name: Dutch Authority for the Financial Markets

organizations.name: Netherlands Authority for Consumers and Markets
organizations.ai_governance_role: Autoriteit Consument & Markt: competition, consumer-protection and sector regulator and Digital Services Coordinator; publishes positions on AI chatbots and algorithms affecting consumers, jointly with the AP.

organizations.name: Netherlands Institute for Human Rights

Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: Backfill run 2026-10-11 in three parts (N1 law via officielebekendmakingen.nl, wetten.overheid.nl and Kamerstukken; N2 government incl. ministry-level search, algorithm framework, register policy and IAMA; N3 regulators AP/DCA/TCA, RDI, AFM, DNB, ACM, CRM), national level only per PROTOCOL §6. Run in parallel with ITA on separate branches. No interruption. The two earlier records were re-checked and retitled (English generative-AI vision dated 2024-01-17; government-wide position dated 2025-01-30, sent to Parliament 2025-04-22); domain-named organisations dropped. EU and CoE instruments are attached via the regional files. AI Act implementation act: consultation draft (internetconsultatie, 20 Apr - 1 Jun 2026), not yet submitted to the Tweede Kamer; no interim designation decree found (lead). Algorithm register: no statutory obligation; governed by the 2023 Verzamelbrief commitments. Algoritmekader accepted on minbzk.github.io because BZK's letter to the Eerste Kamer of 4 Mar 2025 names that address (third-party-host rule). Joint AP-RDI and ACM-AP documents recorded once under the AP. Uber fines not recorded (not about automated decisions). Access: dnb.nl 403 to curl (WebFetch worked), algoritmeregister.overheid.nl proxy 502/DNS failure, Pleio register guide script-rendered, wetten.overheid.nl search 500 (Staatsblad used), datavoorgezondheid.nl 404, RDI document search script-rendered. cyber-security, index-readiness: no material found.

leads.title: SyRI (Systeem Risico Indicatie) — art. 65 Wet SUWI and Besluit SUWI chapter 5a
leads.english_title: SyRI risk-indication system legislation and court judgment
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Social Affairs and Employment; District Court of The Hague
leads.note: Historical. SyRI was based on art. 65 Wet SUWI (Staatsblad 2013, 405) and chapter 5a Besluit SUWI (Staatsblad 2014, 320). The District Court of The Hague (5 February 2020, ECLI:NL:RBDHA:2020:865) held art. 65 SUWI and chapter 5a Besluit SUWI non-binding for breach of art. 8 ECHR. Court judgment kept as a lead only; formal repeal of the provisions was not found in a Staatsblad search for 'SyRI'/'risico-indicatie'. The WGS (recorded) is the later statutory framework for partnership data analysis.

leads.title: Deepfakes in het Wetboek van Strafrecht
leads.note: No AI- or deepfake-specific criminal provision found. Sexual deepfakes are prosecuted under the general offence of making or distributing sexual images without consent (art. 139h Sr, now art. 254ba Sr after the Wet seksuele misdrijven, Staatsblad 2024, 59, in force 1 July 2024); the text does not mention AI. Government policy response to the WODC deepfake studies: Kamerstuk 26643 nr. 1041 (2023). Motion 36264 nr. 13 (Dral/Michon-Derkzen, 15 April 2025) asked for a faster notice-and-takedown procedure for deepfakes. No deepfake bill was before the Tweede Kamer as of 11 October 2026.

leads.title: Tweesporenbeleid 'AI-Decision Support System'
leads.english_title: Two-track policy on AI decision-support systems (Defence)
leads.note: Letter of 29 June 2026 (Tweede Kamer 2026D33525, Kamerstuk 26 643/36 975) setting a two-track policy: build a sovereign European AI-DSS (base expected operational mid-2028) while temporarily continuing current Palantir implementations under three safeguards (Dutch screened staff only, data kept under Dutch control in a private cloud, metadata-only access). Read in full; held as a lead because it is a policy letter in the context of the Defensienota 2026 rather than a standalone policy document.
